citations.M1: `0143` is the contract step and belongs in a later release, not the same window as the expand — ship it days after `state` has run in production
citations.M2: No expand phase: during the ~6-min rolling deploy old pods write `status` only (state NULL, missed by a completed backfill) and new pods write `state` only ... write both columns for one full release, read either.
citations.M3: `mark_paid` silently no-ops while a row has `state` NULL and `status='pending'`: the UPDATE matches 0 rows, the handler still returns 2xx, the provider does not retry
citations.M4: The `CASE` has no `ELSE`, so `PAID` (5210), `canceled` (1988), `complete` (417) and NULL (149) — 7,764 rows ... silently map to NULL
citations.M5: The backfill skips about half the rows: `OFFSET` advances by 5000 while the `state IS NULL` set shrinks by 5000 each batch — switch to keyset paging
citations.M6: The entire loop is inside one `conn.transaction()` — commit per batch, or nothing is resumable and a multi-hour transaction on the primary blocks vacuum
citations.M7: `jobs/nightly_finance_export.py` selects `o.status` and filters `o.status IN ('paid','shipped')`; step 4 breaks the 02:00 UTC export
citations.M8: add a gate between steps 3 and 4: `SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE state IS NULL` must return 0.
citations.M9: The staging log is that bug, not a success: it stops at 211 batches (`done: 1055000`) ... leaving ~1,049,377 staging rows NULL and unnoticed
citations.M10: `0143`'s downgrade recreates an empty `status` column, so the free-text values are gone for good — snapshot `id, status` into a backup table
citations.M11: staging did 1,000,000 rows in 627s ≈ 1,600 rows/s, so 61,437,902 rows is ~10.7 hours at best
citations.M12: `SET NOT NULL` takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and full-scans 61M rows — add `CHECK (state IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID`, `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`, then `SET NOT NULL`
